Parameter Correspondence: ppidyom, ppm, and IDyOM

ParameterCorrespondence.Rmd

This vignette maps every tunable parameter across the three implementations. For each parameter, we first explain what it controls conceptually — in terms of what kind of listener or memory it represents — then give the technical definition, and finally the parameter names in each package.

For the algorithmic discrepancies that go beyond parameter naming see vignette("implementation-discrepancy").

Quick-reference matrix

Concept ppidyom ppm (new_ppm_simple) IDyOM (:stmo / :ltmo)

max context length N order_bound :order-bound

escape method stm_lambda / ltm_lambda ∈ {A,B,C,D,X} escape ∈ {a,b,c,d,ax} :escape ∈ {:a,:b,:c,:d,:x} ¹
exclusion stm_exclusion / ltm_exclusion exclusion :exclusion
update exclusion stm_update_exclusion / ltm_update_exclusion update_exclusion :update-exclusion

mixture exponent b (default 1) — implicit b = 7

For exact working code for each profile see vignette("example-calls").

Decision tree: choosing your parameters

Not sure which parameters you actually need to touch? Work through these questions in order. Most users only need §1–2; the rest are for replication work or deliberate exploration.

What is your goal?

  • General use — analysing music or testing a hypothesis, no numerical replication target. Use the “general use” values throughout.
  • Match ppm — reproduce Harrison’s ppm package numerically. Use the “match ppm” values throughout.
  • Match IDyOM — reproduce IDyOM (Common Lisp) numerically. Use the “match IDyOM” values throughout.
  • Exploring a parameter — e.g. comparing escape methods or order sensitivity. Read the relevant section below; the “general use” values are a safe baseline to vary from.
Parameter General use Match ppm Match IDyOM
model_type pick per §2 "stm" only match :models
N 3–5 match order_bound match :order-bound
ppm_type "interpolation" "interpolation" "interpolation" (or "backoff" for mixtures=nil)
stm_lambda / ltm_lambda "C" match escape match :escape
stm_exclusion TRUE FALSE (ppm default) or match exclusion TRUE (IDyOM default) or match :exclusion
ltm_exclusion TRUE n/a (no LTM) TRUE (IDyOM default) or match :exclusion
stm_update_exclusion TRUE FALSE (ppm default) or match update_exclusion FALSE (IDyOM default) or match :update-exclusion
ltm_update_exclusion FALSE n/a (no LTM) FALSE (IDyOM default) or match :update-exclusion
ltm_start_token TRUE n/a (no LTM) FALSE
idyom_base FALSE FALSE TRUE
b 1 n/a (no mixtures) 7

Model Type model_type

What it represents: PPM models a listener who hears a musical sequence event by event and forms expectations about what comes next. The model type determines what memory that listener draws on:

  • A listener recalling only the current piece — counting how often each pattern has occurred so far in this sequence → STM (short-term model)
  • A listener drawing entirely on accumulated musical experience, encoded from a training corpus before the current piece began → LTM (long-term model)
  • A listener using both simultaneously, blending them according to how confident each is → both / both+

The LTM is built by calling train_sequence() on a corpus before prediction begins. In both/both+ models the STM and LTM distributions are combined using an entropy-weighted geometric mean (see parameter b for the blend exponent).

Research question model_type Needs train_sequence() first? Relevant params
How surprising is this, given only what’s been heard so far in this piece? "stm" No stm_* only
How surprising is this to someone who knows the style, but not this specific piece? "ltm" Yes ltm_* only
Same, but long-term knowledge keeps updating as the piece is heard "ltm+" Yes ltm_* only
How surprising is this to someone who knows the style and is learning this piece, trusting whichever source is currently more confident? "both" Yes stm_*, ltm_*, b
Same, with long-term knowledge also updating online "both+" Yes stm_*, ltm_*, b

ppm has no LTM or mixture support.

Order bound N

What it controls: The length of the context window — how many preceding events the model uses when predicting the next one. A longer window can capture longer-range patterns (e.g. “what note usually follows this exact 5-note run?”), but at the cost of sparser statistics: long specific patterns are rarely repeated exactly, so the model escapes to shorter contexts more often.

Situation Recommendation
No strong reason to deviate N = 3 to 5 (start with 3)
Short sequences, or a large alphabet (e.g. raw pitch, not scale degree) Lower N (2–3) — higher orders rarely find matches and just add escape overhead
Large corpus, want to capture long-range idiomatic patterns Try N = 5+ and compare
Replicating a specific paper Use the N reported there — it must match exactly for numeric comparison
ppidyom ppm IDyOM
N (constructor arg) order_bound :order-bound in :stmo / :ltmo

All three use the same semantics: contexts longer than N are truncated. IDyOM additionally supports order-bound = nil, which activates shortest-deterministic state selection — the model automatically finds the longest reliable context without a fixed bound. ppidyom and ppm always require an explicit integer bound.

Interpolation vs backoff — ppm_type

What it controls: When a given context order has no observations, there are two strategies for assigning probability to the current event:

  • Interpolation blends predictions from all orders simultaneously. Every order contributes — high orders via their counts, low orders via the mass that escapes from above. The result is a smooth distribution even for unseen contexts.
  • Backoff finds the highest order that does have observations and uses only that, renormalising its distribution to sum to 1. Lower orders are ignored unless every higher order has zero counts.
Situation Value
No reason to deviate "interpolation" (default; matches ppm and IDyOM’s default mixtures = t)
Matching IDyOM run with mixtures = nil "backoff"
Want smoother IC trajectories "interpolation"
Want a stricter “most specific context with data wins” model "backoff"

Escape method — stm_lambda / ltm_lambda

What it controls: When the model has never observed a particular context–symbol pair (zero count), it cannot assign probability from that context alone. Instead it escapes — falling back to shorter contexts that have more data. The escape method determines how aggressively this happens: how much probability mass flows down to lower-order models at each level. Escaping more means relying on general patterns; escaping less means staying closer to the specific context even when counts are thin.

Situation Value
No reason to deviate "C" (Witten-Bell; default in ppm, effectively default in IDyOM)
Want the most conservative escaping — trust the specific context even with thin data "A"
Want escape probability directly proportional to how many distinct symbols follow "B"
Want absolute discounting "D"
Want singleton-based escaping (Moffat 1990) "X" — if comparing directly against IDyOM Lisp, call IDyOM with :x, not :ax (see vignette("implementation-discrepancy") §6)

STM and LTM can use different escape methods if you have a specific reason; most users set both the same.

Every escape method answers: given that we have observed C total events in context c, with t distinct following symbols, what fraction of probability mass should escape to the next-shorter context?

ppidyom ppm IDyOM Escape probability Notes
"A" "a" :a 1 / (C + 1) very conservative; escapes rarely
"B" "b" :b t / C escapes in proportion to novelty
"C" "c" :c t / (C + t) — Witten-Bell default; balances novelty and count stability
"D" "d" :d t / (2C) absolute discounting with d = 0.5
"X" "ax" :x ¹ (t₁ + 1) / (C + t₁ + 1) — Moffat 1990 escapes based on singleton count

C = total events in this context; t = distinct symbols seen after this context; t₁ = singletons (symbols seen exactly once).

ppidyom uses uppercase letters; ppm and IDyOM use lowercase. See R/escape.R for the exact formulas.

¹ AX note: IDyOM’s internal AX keyword is :x, not :ax; calling IDyOM with :ax silently falls back to :c behaviour (an IDyOM bug). The IDyOM comparison fixture uses :x to correctly invoke the AX branch.

Exclusion — stm_exclusion / ltm_exclusion

Stops a note from double-dipping. Once the model’s most specific guess (e.g. “after A B A, it’s almost always C”) has claimed a note, exclusion keeps that same note from also grabbing a share of the leftover probability handed down to its more general, less specific fallback guesses — so that leftover only goes to notes still up for grabs. Exclusion never sets a symbol’s probability to zero; it only changes how the leftover probability gets divided up.

Situation Value
No strong reason to deviate — the standard modern PPM setting TRUE (ppidyom default)
Want every context length to guess over the full alphabet, unaware of what other lengths already predicted FALSE
Matching Harrison’s ppm default FALSE
Matching IDyOM default TRUE
ppidyom ppm IDyOM (stmo/ltmo)
stm_exclusion / ltm_exclusion exclusion :exclusion

Base-distribution interaction: the exclusion flag also controls which order −1 formula IDyOM uses. See vignette("implementation-discrepancy") §1–2 for the full explanation.

Update exclusion — stm_update_exclusion / ltm_update_exclusion

Delays learning (not prediction). When on, a pattern’s very first occurrence doesn’t yet count toward predicting that same pattern — the model only starts using it from the second time that pattern occurs onward. This stops a one-off event from making itself look expected the instant it happens.

Situation Value
Want a pattern to start informing predictions only after it repeats at least once (STM default) TRUE
Want every occurrence, including the first, to count immediately FALSE
Matching ppidyom/IDyOM STM defaults stm_update_exclusion = TRUE
Matching ppm, or IDyOM LTM defaults FALSE
No strong preference Use the constructor defaults (stm_update_exclusion = TRUE, ltm_update_exclusion = FALSE)
ppidyom ppm IDyOM (stmo/ltmo)
stm_update_exclusion / ltm_update_exclusion update_exclusion :update-exclusion

LTM start token — ltm_start_token

Only relevant for "ltm", "ltm+", "both", or "both+".

What it controls: When building the long-term model from a training corpus, should position 1 of each training sequence contribute to the count tables? At that position there is no prior context — the preceding N−1 events are undefined — so it can only be counted as an unconditional observation.

Situation Value
Matching ppm conventions, or no reason to deviate TRUE (ppidyom default)
Matching IDyOM FALSE — IDyOM silently skips positions with no preceding context during training
ppidyom ltm_start_token Behaviour Matches
TRUE (default) all positions counted, including those with no preceding context Harrison’s ppm
FALSE positions with undefined context (NA lags) are skipped IDyOM

ppm has no LTM and therefore no equivalent parameter.

Base distribution — idyom_base

What it controls: Every PPM model needs an ultimate fallback prior — the distribution that catches all probability mass that escapes every context order. At this lowest level (order −1), every symbol receives an equal share. But how large that share is depends on how many symbols are considered “possible.” This choice has a surprisingly large effect on IC values, especially early in a sequence (when counts are thin) and in LTM prediction (where the base is fixed from training rather than growing with the test sequence).

Situation Value
Matching ppm, or STM-only work with no replication target FALSE (ppidyom default)
Matching IDyOM in any configuration TRUE
Using LTM/both and want the base prior to reflect the training corpus rather than the shrinking test-sequence count TRUE
ppidyom idyom_base exclusion Formula Matches
FALSE (default) any 1 / (|α| + 1 − |seen in x[1..t-1]|) — shrinks as the test sequence grows ppm
TRUE OFF 1 / |alphabet| — flat uniform over all symbols IDyOM excl=OFF
TRUE ON, STM 1 / (|α| + 1 − t_root_STM) where t_root = distinct symbols seen so far IDyOM STM excl=ON
TRUE ON, LTM/ltm+ 1 / (|α| + 1 − t_root_LTM) where t_root = distinct symbols in training data (fixed) IDyOM LTM excl=ON

The FALSE (ppm-compatible) and STM idyom_base = TRUE rows are numerically identical: t_root_STM equals the number of distinct symbols seen in the test sequence so far by construction. The LTM row differs critically: IDyOM’s base is fixed by the training corpus, not the test sequence. For a LTM trained on all three symbols, the base prior is 1/(3+1-3) = 1.0 — a constant.

Only has a visible numeric effect when exclusion = FALSE, or whenever LTM is involved (training-corpus counts and test-sequence counts diverge). Full explanation with IDyOM source: vignette("implementation-discrepancy") §1–2.

Mixture exponent b (only for "both" / "both+")

What it controls: When blending STM and LTM predictions, how strongly should the model that is more certain (lower entropy) dominate? This is controlled by the exponent b in the entropy-based weighting formula:

wi∝(HiHmax)−b,Hmax=log⁡2|alphabet| w_i \propto \left(\frac{H_i}{H_{\max}}\right)^{-b}, \quad H_{\max} = \log_2 |alphabet|

With b = 1, the blend is relatively equal — both models contribute proportionally to their confidence. With b = 7 (IDyOM’s default), the lower-entropy model almost completely takes over — a nearly winner-take-all blend.

Situation Value
Matching IDyOM b = 7
Want STM and LTM to contribute roughly proportionally to their confidence b = 1 (ppidyom default)
Not using both/both+ not applicable
